outcome: Undetectable rate of anti-PT IgG (< 5 IU/mL)
Seropositivity rate of anti-PT IgG (>= 40 IU/mL)
Recent infection rate of anti-PT IgG (>= 100 IU/mL)
cohort: The study participants were 227 newborn-mother pairs recruited in Xiamen City, China, during an epidemic period of pertussis.
finding: Almost all pregnant women and their newborns in the study had anti-PT IgG levels low enough to suggest susceptibility to pertussis infection, supporting the rationale for maternal immunization.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the prevalence of seropositivity across demographic characteristics, except for delivery mode among newborns.
